sections.title: Player read-aloud
sections.body: You pass the ward pillar and feel a small pop, like a bubble closing behind you. The forest quiets. Friendly voices rise ahead.

sections.title: Scene summary
sections.body: The party enters Hush, a real warm village inside corporate branding.

sections.title: Visible choices
items: Talk to locals
Head to the tavern
Ask for the Custodian
Rush the delivery

sections.title: Player questions
items: What detail in Arrival at Hush tells you the official story is incomplete?
Who notices the human cost first, and how do they show it?
What small object, smell, or sound makes this scene feel real?

sections.title: GM notes
items: Do not make Hush the joke. The branding is the joke; the people are sincere.
Keep player-facing information actionable. Reveal systemic truth through objects, reactions, and consequences before naming it.
Hush hospitality should use the PDF's guest privilege custom: generous, bounded, and vulnerable to exploitation.
Manufactured-threat lens: seed the contradiction, do not explain it. The surface goal stays simple and heroic.
[ADD/GUARANTEED] A Grail "Protection Coverage" invoice hangs on the Clover Co-op wall, overdue and steep.

sections.title: Checks and rolls
items: Presence Arrive respectfully and read local customs. Easy Gain hush_trust +1 on warmth and humility. 10 Cleanly resolve: Arrive respectfully and read local customs. Add a concrete boon, extra clue, or improved position. Success, plus the player names one helpful detail or asks one follow-up question. Success, but the GM exposes a cost, ticks a countdown, or reveals a new pressure tied to Arrival at Hush. The full goal slips, but the party still learns a useful truth or avoids the worst consequence. The GM makes a hard move that follows from the fiction and leaves the next choice visible. Spend Fear to make trust cost time, reveal a local fear, or show a ward symptom that locals have normalized. On mixed or sliding results, reveal information in layers: visible fact, actionable clue, then systemic truth.

sections.title: Clues
items: Local caution They are afraid. They know the ward has been neglected. Hush has survived by knowing when systems fail.
Guaranteed seed A Grail "Protection Coverage" invoice hangs on the Clover Co-op wall, overdue and steep. A Grail "Protection Coverage" invoice hangs on the Clover Co-op wall, overdue and steep.

sections.title: Loot
items: Clover Co-op gift table if trust is earned
Shoe-line trinket: a tiny local object appears in a PC's boots and hints at a coming challenge.
Sableleaf Shoes: A pair of shoes sewn entirely from broad sablewood leaves sits light as breath, green-veined, and already leaning toward motion.
Sable Sap: Warm amber sap beads from a crack in a huge trunk like the tree is breathing it out. It smells of honey, woodsmoke, and something older.
Tamsin's Home-Token: A small thumb-polished token on a cord hangs beside the torn blue scarf, warm from wear and etched with a tiny house mark instead of a company seal.

sections.title: Mechanics
items: Plot So Far: The party is in Act Three pressure: The party enters Hush, a real warm village inside corporate branding.

Mechanics In Play: Use Daggerheart Duality Dice as baseline. Use the listed Difficulty and outcome options when a roll matters. Keep trivial actions no-roll; roll only when uncertainty, cost, or danger is interesting.

Roll Cards: s03-01-read-the-ward-boundary S03-01 Read the ward boundary Read the ward boundary Knowledge Instinct Knowledge Instinct 13 Knowledge reads old symbols; Instinct feels the boundary pop. Hush becomes a service endpoint instead of a home. Critical Success: best possible version of the action; gain Hope and clear 1 Stress. Add an extra benefit that follows from the fiction. Success with Hope: the PC gets what they wanted and gains Hope. Keep the position clean or generous. Success with Fear: the PC gets what they wanted, but the GM gains Fear and introduces a cost, complication, or pressure. Failure with Hope: the PC does not get the full result, but gains Hope and receives a useful thread, clue, or safer next option. Failure with Fear: the PC fails and the GM gains Fear. Make a hard move that follows from the fiction. Hush becomes a service endpoint instead of a home. Use a hard...
Gm Fear Spends: Make trust cost time, humility, or a public apology. Show a ward symptom locals have normalized because nobody official listened.
Conditions Hazards: No official condition unless a feature, hazard, or fictional position calls for Hidden, Restrained, or Vulnerable.
Search Loot Clues: No fixed loot. Offer clue, texture, or hospitality only when the fiction supports it.
No Roll Guidance: Do not call for a roll when the players have time, a clear method, and no meaningful pressure.
Escalation: Escalate by making cost visible: time, noise, trust, ward instability, or someone vulnerable in danger.
Deescalation: De-escalate through respect, care, honest testimony, useful evidence, or a concrete concession.
Tv Mechanics Caption: Public cue: Arrival at Hush asks what the party does, what it costs, and who is protected.

Trait Variety Note: Primary traits in this scene: Instinct, Knowledge, Presence. If rolls drift toward Instinct/Presence, ask whether Agility, Strength, Finesse, or Knowledge better describes the action.

Class Community Ancestry Reveals: Loreborne: spots older legal, heraldic, or ward-craft language under the branding. Underborne: notices service doors, hidden routes, and who built the thing nobody credits. Highborne: reads etiquette, class panic, and reputational risk. Ridgeborne: notices stonework, weight, pressure, and structural weakness. Wildborne: reads the land, animals, and local ecological stress. Elf/Ribbet/Human/Giant/Katari: invite one sensory or social detail from the player's heritage. Sorcerer/Rogue/Warrior/Guardian/Ranger: give each class one table-facing way to shine without changing the plot.
